summary: No source code changes in diff — only build artifacts and line ending normalization. Four user-requested features from prior review remain unimplemented: OTP authentication (auth still uses email verification tokens), name-only widget creation (forms require domain input), prominent Create Widget button (exists but small text competing with header elements), and settings page widget management (shows workspace config only).
findings: OTP authentication not implemented — Registration endpoint calls createEmailVerificationToken and sends clickable verification URL. User requested 'for signup dont send link to the email just send otp and verify that otp'. Database has emailVerificationOtp and otpExpiry fields but they are unused. Implement OTP generation (6-digit code), store in user record with expiry, send code in email body, create /auth/verify-otp endpoint, update signup UI to show OTP input field.

Widget creation requires domain — All widget creation forms (dashboard-pages.tsx line 509, onboarding.tsx line 166, management-pages.tsx) require both name and domain fields with 'required' attribute. User requested 'create a widget without asking any site url ohk just name'. Remove domain field or make optional with auto-generated placeholder.

Create Widget button not prominent — Button in dashboard-shell.tsx lines 230-236 has gradient styling but uses text-sm (small), hidden sm:flex (mobile hidden), and competes with workspace selector, notifications, and profile in header. User requested 'in top right create new widget' with emphasis implying primary CTA. Increase visual weight: larger size, stronger shadow, or floating position separate from header controls.

Settings page lacks widget management — WorkspaceSettingsPage in management-pages.tsx line 290 shows workspace name, timezone, language, data retention only. User requested 'in settings show all widget name and there settings like widgetid1 set what i want to ask and some question on top'. Add section listing all widgets with per-widget config UI: widget name, ID, welcome message, position, colors, and quick questions management.
